title: AQ Podcast | Is Latin America Poised for Takeoff?
author: OCTOBER 1, 2026
text:
FacebookXLinkedInThreadsEmailShare

Reading Time: < 1 minute
Latin America is having its best economic outlook since the commodities boom of the 2000s. Record commodity prices, a weak U.S. dollar, a privileged position in the global trade war—selling to both the U.S. and China—and a wave of business-friendly governments are creating conditions the region hasn’t seen in decades. But Latin America has defied rosy predictions before, and the outlook remains uncertain in its three largest economies: Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina. 

Today on the podcast, we ask what a new takeoff would mean in practical terms for growth, the markets, and its citizens; take stock of the region’s most relevant economies; and examine what could prevent this favorable moment from becoming a lasting reality.

Our guest is Ernesto Revilla, chief economist for Latin America at Citi and a member of AQ’s editorial board.
